Messages.Author: John
Messages.Body:
this recently came up...

Minion A declines to maneuver (Acting)
Minion B declines to maneuver
Minion A maneuvers

Now at this point at least two of us at the table started screaming (well
not literally, but we quickly objected) to which the player controlling the
acting minion said "Where does it say that". The online rulebook was
consulted as well as three different editions of the rule books, rulings
were quickly searched, etc

What is boils down to is: that despite being certain that there is a rule
somewhere preventing this, we could not find it.

If someone could point me in the right direction (or correct me if I'm
totally out to lunch) of where to find said ruling it would be greatly
appreciated.

-JTP

Messages.Author: Kevin M.
Messages.Body:

news:vBrQ8.46631$s82.3...@news1.calgary.shaw.ca...


Hey, I'll take a shot at this, as I had to look it up one time, and this is
what I used:

(IANLSJ, and the *notable text indicators* have been inserted by me.)

-~-~-~-~-~-
1.6.1 [6.] Sequencing
If two or more players want to play a card or effect, the acting Methuselah
plays first. At every stage, the acting player always has the opportunity to
play the next card or effect. So after playing one effect, she may play another
and another. *Once she is finished*, the opportunity passes to the defending
Methuselah (in the cases of directed actions and combat), then to the rest of
the Methuselahs in clockwise order from the acting Methuselah. Note that *if
any card or effect is used by any Methuselah*, the acting Methuselah again gets
the opportunity to play the next effect.
-~-~-~-~-~-

So:

- Methuselah A's minion (acting) chooses to not maneuver.
- Methuselah B's minion chooses not to maneuver.
- Methuselah A's minion cannot now maneuver, since no card or effect has been
used by any Methuselah in the Determine Range step (which is the only way that
the step can "continue", aside from explicit card text).
- Determine Range step ends.

That's what I used as a "ruling".

Not really, meth A might be able to fight at close or long and say "I don't
manuver" to see if meth B manuvers, indicating his preference for long
range, in which case meth A will probably choose to attempt to make the
combat short range to try to muck up meth B's combat plan. This is
particularly relevant when meth B is play with cards that are only useable
at a specific range.

e.g. Meth A is playing Potence/Celerity and has a Pushing the Limits and a
Thrown Sewer Lid ( and no dodge/prevent ). Meth B is playing Tzimisce.
Meth A has a delemma, go for range and risk a Breath of the Dragon or go for
close and risk a Blood of Acid and/or agg hand strike.

Meth A would quite possibly manuver out with the Gate, hopoing to avoid
Blood of Acid/agg hand strike unplesantness, only to get Breath of the
Dragoned.

On the other hand, if you could do what we're discussing.

Meth A says "I don't manuver" and Meth B manuvers out, Meth A now can be
pretty sure that Meth B has a BotD and will probably manuver in with the
Gate. Leaving Meth B needing another manuver or taking agg damage from his
own BotD ( or needing a 3rd card to get an agg hand strike ). I'd say Meth A
has gained an advantage. Meth B has had to use a manuver he otherwise might
not have had to.

Messages.Author: LSJ
Messages.Body:
John wrote:
> Acting minion plays a bleed action and declares is done playing effects
> Target methuselah declines to block
> Now since target methuselah has decided not to block, he/she has not been
> "reacted to", so can the acting methuselah play conditioning? Or is he
> "done" playing effects? Or is the decision to not block sufficient of an
> even for the acting minion to again be permitted to play action modifiers.

The decision not to block is an event.
After that event, the acting Methuselah gets the next chance to play the
next effect. She could play Conditioning at that point.
